title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness and starvation prevention (timeouts)
author: Marco Ruiz
description:
Motivation: production traces and perf lab runs showed that the continuous-batcher scheduler could unfairly favor certain request classes under high concurrency and long-tail sequences. Symptoms: increased p99 latency for small, latency-sensitive requests and occasional starvation of low-throughput tenants when large KV-cache warmup requests flooded the queue. This PR introduces conservative scheduler tuning and targeted fixes to improve queueing fairness, add starvation prevention policies, and introduce adaptive timeouts to protect latency SLOs.

Changes (high level): 1) Introduce a multi-queue sharding strategy in the continuous-batcher scheduler to separate short-latency requests from long-running KV-warmup and large-batch requests; 2) Add per-queue starvation detectors that escalate priority for queues that have been deferred > configurable threshold; 3) Implement adaptive enqueue timeouts to bound end-to-end waiting time and fall back to a lower-cost model variant when timeouts occur; 4) Tighten fairness accounting by switching from proportional size-based tokens to a hybrid token+age scoring function; 5) Add metrics and tracing hooks for queue depth, per-queue oldest-request-age, and timeout events.

Checklist: - [x] Scheduler queue sharding and routing logic implemented - [x] Starvation detector and priority escalation - [x] Adaptive enqueue timeout + fallback policy - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Performance benchmarks and ci gating - [x] Docs and migration notes

Notes on configuration: default behavior is backward-compatible; new controls are behind feature flags and runtime config (continuous_batcher.queue_sharding=true, continuous_batcher.starvation_threshold_ms=1200, continuous_batcher.enqueue_timeout_ms=800). We tuned defaults after lab experimentation to reduce regressions on mixed workloads.

Benchmark results (summary): In the perf lab (multi-tenant mixed workload with 70% short-chat, 20% long-generation, 10% KV-warmup): p50 unchanged, p95 improved by ~10%, p99 improved from 145ms -> 118ms (~18.6% improvement) for latency-sensitive traffic; tail starvation events (requests deferred > 2s) reduced by 92%. Overall token throughput unchanged (within 2% variance).

Risk and rollback: changes are incremental and feature-flagged. If unintended regressions are observed, flip continuous_batcher.queue_sharding=false to restore previous single-queue behavior.

Related: ENG-12458 documented the customer-facing symptom, ENG-12501 is the follow-up for tuning for Dedicated clusters.
